The area of one loop of the polar curve $r=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )$ is given by the integral

$$
A=\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}{sin}^{2}⁡(5\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Which of the following represents the total area bounded by the polar curve?
question.worked_solution:
The given polar curve is the polar rose with $5$ petals, and we know that the area of the first petal is

$$
A=\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}{sin}^{2}⁡(5\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14253263/assets/53d86dd26966e3e4b5a75441fc7a1d6ab8f2244097f61677086f5783495ed6cb.png)

The $1$st petal is traversed from ${\theta }_{1}=0$ to ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{5},$ and the length of this interval is $\frac{\pi }{5}.$

To find the interval for the second petal, we have to add $\frac{\pi }{5}$ to both ends of the interval of the first petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{3} & ={\theta }_{1}+\frac{\pi }{5}=0+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{5} \\ {\theta }_{4} & ={\theta }_{2}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{5}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{2\pi }{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, to obtain the interval for the third petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{5}$ to both ends of the interval of the second petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{5} & ={\theta }_{3}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{5}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{2\pi }{5} \\ {\theta }_{6} & ={\theta }_{4}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{2\pi }{5}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{3\pi }{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the interval for the fourth petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{5}$ to both ends of the interval of the third petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{7} & ={\theta }_{5}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{2\pi }{5}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{3\pi }{5} \\ {\theta }_{8} & ={\theta }_{6}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{3\pi }{5}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{4\pi }{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the interval for the fifth petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{5}$ to both ends of the interval of the fourth petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{9} & ={\theta }_{7}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{3\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{4\pi }{5} \\ {\theta }_{10} & ={\theta }_{8}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{4\pi }{5}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, we obtain the following intervals for all $5$ petals of our rose:

$$
{{[0,\frac{\pi }{5}]}_{⏟}}_{1\text{st}},\,{{[\frac{\pi }{5},\frac{2\pi }{5}]}_{⏟}}_{2\text{nd}},\,{{[\frac{2\pi }{5},\frac{3\pi }{5}]}_{⏟}}_{3\text{rd}},\,{{[\frac{3\pi }{5},\frac{4\pi }{5}]}_{⏟}}_{4\text{th}},\,{{[\frac{4\pi }{5},\pi ]}_{⏟}}_{5\text{th}}
$$

Therefore, the total area of the given polar curve can be obtained if the curve is traversed from $\theta =0$ to $\theta =\pi :$

$$
{A}_{\text{total}}=\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡(5\theta )\,\text{d}\theta 
$$
